note: Reconstructed from evals/2026-09-16-implementer-security-review-trigger.md: its eight cases, one for one. The original ran real `claude -p --agent implementer` sessions and read the stream-json transcript for a Skill(security-review) call. This set runs the agent as a proxy — a general-purpose subagent given agents/implementer.md — which has no Skill tool for this plugin's skills, so the observable stand-in is reading skills/security-review/SKILL.md, recorded in transcript.md. Every result from this set says `proxy`. The expectations were rewritten after iteration 1 on the graders' critique, as run-evals' behavioral loop step 7 requires. Four graders independently found that the negative arm's "records no reading of security-review/SKILL.md" contradicts the agent's own Security step, which decides from that skill's frontmatter description — so the check is now against the SKILL.md *body*. The rest: the test expectation no longer passes on a stub, the unsupported-claim check covers the whole run rather than the final message alone, the negative arm's length budget is split from its decision clause, and the positive arm gained an expectation graded from outputs/ alone, since every other one grades prose the executor writes about itself. 2026-09-20's pass rates were measured against the wording before this revision; that wording is quoted in the eval log.
